releases.notes:
- **Fixed:** the render scale (`RenderSettings.RenderScale`, `BURROW_RENDER_SCALE`, `-render-scale`) was silently ignored in hybrid frames (voxels plus scene meshes: any game with a held item, an animal or another player), which rendered at native size and also lost the SMAA the scaled request had replaced with FSR 1. The mesh phases already run inside the voxel main pass with its render-size viewport and camera, the object velocity pass is recorded at the render size and the canvas is drawn by the composite at the display size, so `effectiveAA` no longer forces native there. Measured on an M2 Max at ultra, 3456x2008: native 24.8 fps (GPU 40 ms), 75 % 36.9 fps (27 ms), 50 % 49.2 fps (17.6 ms).
- **Changed (performance):** per-chunk draws of the main and shadow passes are recorded by one cgo call per pipeline (`vulkan.CmdChunkDraws`, `third_party_vulkan/chunk_draws.go`): the loop in C rebinds the buffer and pushes the constants only when they change, instead of four cgo calls per draw. About 6 % less main-thread time in `recordVoxelPass` at ~2 500 draws; the rest is MoltenVK's own work per draw.

- **Added:** a dedicated server pauses when nobody plays, as Minecraft's `pause-when-empty-seconds`. `server.json` `pause_when_empty_seconds` (60 by default, absent in an old file = 60; 0 = never): once no player has been connected for that long the server saves the world and runs no tick (no CPU, the world and its clock wait; autosave skipped while paused), connections are still accepted and the ticks resume as soon as a player is authenticated, without catching up the paused time. `replica.ServerConfig.PauseWhenEmpty`, `Server.Idle`, `netplay.HostOptions.PauseWhenEmpty`, `netplay.Server.Idle`; `status` reports `paused`. Tests `TestPauseWhenEmpty`, `TestConfigDefaults`. Branch `dedicated-pause-when-empty`.
- **Added:** linked custom blocks (`links`, `link_faces`, `arms` in `blocks/custom_blocks.json`; `shape.CustomSpec.Links`, `LinkFaces`, `Arms`; `DeriveLink`): a block joins named link groups (at most 32 per project, `Model.Link` mask) and connects on a face to a neighbour that shares a group when both allow the faces between them (`Model.LinkFaces`, authored facing north and turned with `facing`; `Model.Links`). With `arms` it has 64 derived variants, its boxes plus the arm boxes of each connected face (collision, selection, look), so a pipe, a cable or a shaft shows a branch toward each connected neighbour only; a block with `links` and no arms (a pump, a machine) keeps one look and makes its neighbours reach it. Nothing is stored: a save keeps one state per block, ids do not move. Validation: arms need links, arms only on allowed faces, model plus arms within 32 boxes, not with planes or round. Tests `TestLinkedPipeBranchesTowardItsGroupOnly`, `TestLinkedShaftLinksAlongItsAxisTurnedWithFacing`, `TestLinksAreValidated`. Branch `gogame-block-links`.
- **Added:** moon phases in the HDR sky. `engine.RenderSettings.MoonPhases` / `MoonPhase` (lunar age as a fraction of the cycle: 0 new, 0.25 first quarter, 0.5 full, 0.75 last quarter; `Renderer.SetMoonPhase`) draw the disc lit on the side of its phase (waxing on the right, a faint earthshine on the dark side, `shaders/atmo.glsl`, carried by the free `S.fx.x`), and the moonlight follows it: direct light and moonlit ambient (`scene.Sky.AtmoMoon`, `scene.MoonLight`: 12 % of the full moon's at a new moon), the moon's light on clouds and on falling water. Off by default (a full moon, as before). Capture aids `BURROW_MOON=<age>` and `BURROW_SKY_TIME=<0..1>`. Rebuilt `sky_hdr.frag.spv`, `water_hdr.frag.spv`. Tests `TestMoonLightFollowsThePhase`, `TestMoonPhaseUniform`. Branch `gogame-moon-phase`.
- **Added:** local weather (`weather.LocalWeather`, `weather/local.go`): the installed `Climate` may also implement `WeatherOverride(seed, x, y, z, clock) (kind, intensity, ok)`, which `At` asks first. `KindClear` stops any precipitation there (even under a raining front; cover at most 0.25, no fog), `KindCloudy` is overcast and dry, `KindFog` dense fog, rain kinds and `KindSnow` fall with the given intensity (rain or snow by the temperature, `Lightning` in a storm). `Local.Override` reports it. State, hash and snapshots are unchanged. `RenderFX` takes the cloud cover, overcast, sunlight, wetness and fog from the camera's place when it is overridden (before, only the precipitation and the fog density followed the place, the sky followed the front), and a local storm under a front that is not a storm draws flashes from the seed and the clock. Tests `TestLocalWeatherDisks`, `TestLocalWeatherRender`. Branch `gogame-weather-local`.
- **Added:** flying creatures in the built-in brain actions (`nav/fly.go`). A `flyer` agent without `physics.character` was already moved in 3D by the plugin (no gravity, 26-neighbour A*); `wander`, `flee` and the new `hover {alt,tol}` now keep a cruising height of `alt` metres above the ground under the agent (`World.Ground`: the first solid, micro or liquid cell below; a roof lowers it), the argument falling back on the blackboard number `fly_alt` (`nav.FlyAltKey`) that rules set with `Ctx.SetBlackboard`; `wander` jitters it by `alt_var` metres, `flee` never descends, `hover` climbs or sinks to it and stops. `chase`, `move_to` and `look_home` take `above` (metres over their point). Without `alt`/`fly_alt` nothing changes. Flyers that do not swim no longer enter whole liquid cells. Tests `TestFlyerGoalOverAWall`, `TestFlyerHoverKeepsCruisingHeight`, `TestFlyerWandersAndFleesAloft`, `TestGroundAndFlyersAvoidWater`, `TestNavFlyer`. Branch `gogame-nav-fly`.
- **Fixed:** a world reloaded from a save put the player back at the spawn point. The first person controller is built at its start position before the save is restored, and its first pose sync wrote that position over the restored player node (`syncPose` adopts the node only once it has synced). `Controller.AdoptPlayerNode` takes the node's pose, called by an `OnRestore` hook installed in `internal/game` after the app is built. Test `TestControllerTakesTheRestoredPlayerPosition`.
- **Fixed:** a node moved by a visual delta (`visual.bind`, `visual.sway`, `Frame.VisualAdd`...) under another moved node outside any held subtree took only its own delta: a wing flapping on a bird carried by a bound orbit stayed where the scene put it while the body flew. The deltas now compose like a rig, as they did under a `render.viewattach` node (`worldDeltaMatrix`, `engine/render_world.go`): each turns its node around its own pivot and the moves of its moved ancestors apply after it. Test `TestVisualDeltaOnAChildOfAMovedWorldNode`. Branch `gogame-visual-nested`.
- **Added:** grid-to-grid transfers in `gameui` (`Node.Transfer`, `"transfer": true`): an item dragged, or picked with a click, from one grid and put on a cell of another grid that also has `transfer` emits `transfer` on the source grid (`Index` its cell, `To` the cell there, `Value` the other grid's id, then `:half` for half a stack picked with a right click, `:one` for one item put with a right click, the rest staying carried). Before, a drag that left its grid was cancelled and a click on another grid only selected there. Grids without the field behave as before. Test `TestGridTransfer`. Branch `gogame-grid-transfer`.
- **Added:** knockback as a velocity, as Minecraft sends the velocity of a hit. `netsim.Push(e, id, vx, vy, vz)` (and `gogame.Ctx.PushPlayer`): for a client that claims its position the push is recorded in the replicated registry (`Player.KickSeq`, `Kick`), the client adds it to its own walk when it sees the count change (`predictor.kicked`) and its budgets grow by what the push may carry it, so the knockback is smooth and never a correction; a player the server walks itself gets it in the server's walk (`Player.Knock`). `WalkState.KX/KZ`: a knockback added to the walk that fades by 0.62 every 1/20 s (the game's own knockback). Registry flags 32 (KickSeq, Kick, Knock) and 64 (Claims). Before, a knockback moved the node from the rules: one correction per tick while it lasted. Tests `TestPushIsAppliedByTheClaimingClient`, `TestPushMovesAPlayerTheServerWalks`, `TestPushedClientIsNeverCorrected`.
- **Added:** `BURROW_NET_LAG=<ms>[,<jitter ms>]` on a client (`transport.WithLag`, `NewLag`, `net/transport/lag.go`): delays both directions of a real connection, order kept, to try a network game with the latency of the internet on one machine. Test `TestLagDelaysAndKeepsOrder`. Measured with it (75 ± 20 ms each way, a windowed client running in circles for 40 s on a local dedicated server): 1262 inputs, all claims taken, no correction.
- **Fixed (tests):** `TestReplicatedLoopback` and `TestVoiceLoopback` moved their guests by the view they report, which the server no longer follows when the player has a node (it centers the interest on the node, `centerOf`): they place the players' nodes (`placePlayer`).
- **Changed:** movement authority, as in Minecraft. A predicting client now sends with every input where its own walk put the player (`netsim.Input` `px/py/pz/pvy/hp/tp`, `netsim.WithClaim`) and the server takes that position when it is plausible (`net/netsim/authority.go`, `claimOK`): a horizontal distance budget refilled every tick at the fastest allowed speed (×1.4, one second of burst), the climb allowed off the ground, a liquid or a ladder (`Rise`: 1.25 jump heights plus a step), the vertical speed, and the body box swept from the node to the claim (vertical then horizontal, or the reverse) must reach it. Before, the server walked every input itself and the client was corrected (rolled back and replayed) as soon as the two disagreed. Now the server answers with a teleport (`netsim.Player.TP`, replicated in the public registry) only when it moved the node itself (a game rule: knockback, teleport, mount, respawn: the node is not where the last input left it, `Player.Last`) or refused a claim (it then walks that input itself); the inputs computed before the client saw the teleport are walked by the server, and the client (`internal/netplay/predict.go`) snaps and replays only on a new teleport number. Inputs without a claim (other clients, lockstep, tests) are walked as before. The registry encoding gains flags 8 (TP, Rise, Budget, BudgetTick) and 16 (Last), absent while zero: older states decode and hash unchanged. Measured with a windowed client on a local dedicated server, running in circles for 40 s: 1278 inputs, all claims taken, no correction. Tests `TestHonestClaimsAreNeverCorrected`, `TestCheatedClaimsAreRefused` (speed, wall, flight), `TestServerMoveIsATeleport`, `TestAuthorityStateRoundTrips`, `TestPredictionMatchesTheServerExactly` (claims).
- **Fixed:** a replicated client animated everything by the integer tick of the last server frame (`FrameState.Tick`, set by `ReplicaSetTick` when a frame arrives): rain and snow streaks, water waves and swell, swaying leaves, clouds and animated textures stood still on most frames and jumped when frames came, unevenly (measured on a client at ~107 frames per second: 81 % of frames without motion, 19 ticks/s ± 40). The renderer now draws with a smooth animation clock (`render/vulkan/animclock.go`, as a Minecraft client ticks its own time between the server's updates): it advances with the wall clock between ticks, follows the tick without going back, freezes at most 2 ticks past the last one, stays exactly on a fixed tick (tests, frozen screenshots) and snaps on a jump; same measure after: 0 % of frames still, 20.0 ticks/s ± 0.4. Test `TestAnimClockIsSmoothBetweenBurstyTicks`. Branch `gogame-smooth-anim-time`.
- **Fixed:** the weather of a replicated client (sent every 20 ticks) drew its day clock as received: the rain cells, which drift with the clock, and the sky moved 20 ticks at a time. `weather.Plugin` advances the drawn clock with the ticks between two states, only for a clock seen running at one per tick and at most 40 ticks past the last state (`clientClock`, `weather/plugin.go`). Test `TestClientClockRunsBetweenServerStates`.
- **Added:** predicted blocks on a replicated client. `replica.Client.PredictBlocks` (`net/replica/predict_blocks.go`) writes a guess into the replicated world at the next `Poll` and remembers the server's block under it; before every server frame the guessed cells go back to that truth (the frame applies to the server's state exactly), after it the truth is read again and the guess written back until the server acknowledged a later input (plus 4 frames) or 1.5 s passed: the cell then keeps what the server says (the block if a rule wrote it, the old one if it refused). `gogame.Frame.PredictVoxels` (no-op alone), and the window twins of the rules' helpers on the replicated copy: `Frame.RaycastShaped`, `Frame.PlaceStates`, `Frame.ToggleStates` (`gogame/framepredict.go`); `gogame.Client.PredictVoxels` for windowless clients (tests). Tests `TestPredictedBlocksYieldToTheServer` (replica); the game tests it end to end with its rules.
- **Added:** `weather.Climate` / `weather.SetClimate` (`weather/climate.go`): a project gives the temperature and humidity of each place (its biomes, seasons, relief) and the per-position sampler uses them instead of `worldgen.ClimateAt`. A precipitating front then falls in rain cells (value noise of 260 blocks, 110 for a storm) that drift with the prevailing wind (4 m/s, mostly eastward, turned by the seed), covering about 10 % of a dry land up to 70 % of a wet one (a desert, humidity under 0.12, sees a shower now and then; a saturated air, humidity above 0.9, rains over the whole front, as a continuous stratiform rain); rain or snow by the place's temperature as before. Only `At` reads it: state, hash and snapshots are unchanged. Test `TestClimateRainCells`.
- **Added:** `gogame.Ctx.Weather(x, y, z)` (the `weather.Local` of a block, for the rules), `Ctx.WeatherFront()` and `Ctx.SetWeather(weather.Set)` (a `weather_set` from the rules: a game that freezes the automatic fronts and starts its own).
- **Changed (performance):** the HDR main pass no longer draws all terrain with one discarding pipeline. The solid range of the chunks that are not cross-fading is drawn first with `voxel_hdr_solid.frag` (`NO_DISCARD`: a shader that may discard turns off the early depth test and the hidden surface removal of tile-based GPUs for everything it draws); the cut-out range (leaves, grass, flowers, custom planes) then gets a depth prepass (`voxel_hdr_pre.frag`, `DEPTH_PREPASS`: the alpha test alone, no colour written: `pipeDesc.noColor`) and is shaded at depth EQUAL without discard (`pipeDesc.depthEqual`), so each visible foliage pixel is shaded once; cross-fading chunks and the slice view keep the discarding pipeline. `BURROW_LEAF_PREPASS=0` turns the prepass off. Measured in a forest overview (M2 Max, 1280x720, ultra): 22-24 ms GPU -> 14.3 ms (solid split alone: -1.2 ms), images identical; the low/medium non-HDR levels are unchanged. Tried and dropped (no measurable gain): back-face culling in the shadow pass, skipping the sun shadow taps for empty cut-out texels.
- **Added:** custom block planes attached to a face (`plane_cull` in `blocks/custom_blocks.json`, `shape.CustomSpec.PlaneCull`): such a plane is hidden when a solid neighbour covers that face and lit as that face; a plane lying flat on the whole face is drawn single-sided, facing out, and stays drawn next to another such block (Minecraft's fancy leaves: through the holes the deeper leaves show); a tilted plane attached to a face (`Quad.Tuft`) is also hidden when the neighbour has planes attached to its facing side (`Model.Shell`), so tufts show only where the face is in the open. Such planes cover nothing (a trunk behind holey leaves keeps its faces). `quadHidden` takes the footprint of a plane that leaves the cell within the face. Test `TestPlanesAttachedToAFaceHideBetweenNeighbours`.
- **Added:** connected textures per face (`mesh.ConnectedFaceProvider`, `BlockTextures.ConnectedFaceLayers`): a block without whole-block variants whose face texture X has `X_ctm_0..15` (a grass block's top, its dirt bottom) takes them on that face only, faces with a tinted overlay excepted; the face keeps its tint (biome), where whole-block variants are untinted. The variants of one texture are shared by every block.
- **Added:** `round` (custom blocks, `shape.CustomSpec.Round`, `DeriveRound`): a cube whose open edges are chamfered by that many sixteenths, 64 variants keyed by which faces are closed (a solid face, or another block with attached planes): an open face is inset along each edge it shares with another open face, a bevel covers that edge, a corner triangle closes three open faces; a face closed by such a neighbour stays whole (seen through the holes of a cut-out texture), so two blocks side by side show no groove. Every quad is attached to its face (lit as it, AO); the block has Shell on all faces. Test `TestRoundBlocksChamferOnlyOpenEdges`. The chamfers carry the normal of one of their faces (six normals only): a foliage fragment offsets its shadow lookup toward the sun instead of along its face (`voxel_body.glsl`), or the chamfers shadowed themselves (streaks along the edges and corners of round leaves). A bevel maps the texture at its own scale (a window as wide as the bevel; the whole texture squeezed into a strip drew stretched streaks along every edge). The cut-out mip bias (`CutoutMipBias`) is not applied to a project's foliage (`vFoliage`), whose leaf faces are nearly full: the earlier mips smeared them into streaks at grazing angles. Only the horizontal edges (with the top or the bottom) are chamfered (`roundVertical` off: the narrow bevels of the vertical edges, seen slantwise and moved by the wind, flickered without a temporal AA, ~300 flickering pixels a frame against ~80 with sharp leaves; now ~78). Where the neighbour across the end of a chamfered edge is not chamfered along it (a block over one of the two faces), the bevel stops short and the block keeps a square corner flush with it (`Model.RoundQuads`, square bits from `Mesher.roundSquare`, geometry cached per key).
- **Added:** `plane_cover` (custom blocks, `shape.CustomSpec.PlaneCover`): opaque planes lying flat on the faces (`plane_cull`) cover those faces, so nothing is drawn between two such blocks and a neighbour's face against them neither (a dense leaf cube draws its skin only). Test `TestPlaneCoverHidesFacesBetweenNeighbours`.
- **Fixed:** the soft sun shadow of the shader levels rotated its taps by a per-pixel noise that only a temporal anti-aliasing averages; without one (SMAA, FXAA, off) every penumbra showed a fine checker that crawled with the camera (plant and leaf shadows were all checker). Without a temporal frame (`aaInfo.y`) the rotation is fixed: a smooth penumbra that holds still (`sunShadow`, `common.glsl`). Foliage of a project (`vFoliage`) takes more ambient on its undersides and sides (`ambK`): the underside of a crown came out near black.
- **Changed:** foliage of custom blocks (planes, `translucency: "foliage"`) sways in the wind like cube leaves (`SwayKind`: leaves, was static) and is known to the shaders whatever its texture: a per-block table (`Renderer.foliageTable`, from `Options.Sway`, built even without sway) sets bit 15 of the packed z (`vFoliage` in `voxel.vert` / `voxel_body.glsl`). Such foliage is lit by face like a block (top bright, sides and underside darker) with a real ambient occlusion: planes attached to a face get the corner occlusion of a cube face, solid blocks and blocks with attached planes counting as occluders (`Mesher.planeAO`, was a constant 3), taken strong in the shader (0.4..1); it keeps the contrast of its texture and almost one hue (the foliage lift and the per-block hue and brightness shifts are mostly off for it: a crown read as a patchwork of cubes). The sun shadow of every terrain fragment is read at its position before the wind sway (`vStill`): the shadow pass does not sway, so light and shade crawled over moving leaves. A first try lighting foliage regardless of its facing (as the Minecraft shader packs do) was dropped: crowns came out flat.
- **Added:** `worldgen.CurrentSource` (`CurrentAt(seed, x, y, z) (fx, fz, ok)`): a generator says which way its still water runs. A river generated at one level has no head difference, so `LiquidTable.Flow` gave a pond: no drift, or random swirls where fine water woke up. `engine.SetBiomeGen` installs it (unwrapped like the tint source) through `mesh.SetCurrent`, and the liquid surface mesher (`mesh/liquidsurf.go`) uses it on a source cell under open air that has no flow of its own; the surface then drifts with it (`FineVertex.Flow`). Water with a head difference keeps its own flow. Test `TestStillWaterTakesTheInstalledCurrent`.
- **Changed:** water colour (HDR `water_hdr.frag`, and `water.glsl`): the scattering albedo is a muted green-teal (was a saturated blue), the biome tint weighs more in absorption (0.7, was 0.4) and scattering (0.55, was 0.25), a grey turbidity term (0.14 per block) fades the bottom into the water's own colour over a few blocks, in-scatter 0.42 (was 0.28); the non-HDR water mixes less of its fixed turquoise and saturates less. Natural water instead of a swimming-pool blue.
- **Added:** `VoxelWorld.Remesh()`: rebuild every resident chunk mesh (old meshes stay until replaced), for a change the engine cannot see, such as a `TintSource` whose colours follow the game's seasons.
- **Added:** text editing in `gameui` input fields: selection (Shift+arrows, Shift+Home/End, drag with the mouse, double click = word, triple click = all), select all / cut (Ctrl/Cmd+A, X; C copies the selection), moves and deletions by word (Alt on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) and to the ends (Cmd on macOS), typing replaces the selection, the text scrolls so the caret stays visible (`Widget.TextScroll`), `Widget.Caret` / `Selection`, `UI.FocusedSelection`, and `UI.TextMeasure` (a skin that draws the text in another font gives its measure: the caret lands under the pointer). A bound value changed by the game while the field has the focus now shows. Test `TestTextFieldEditing`.
- **Fixed:** a click in an input field emitted "submit" and app actions ran on "change" events: a field whose action is `world:create` or `net:join` created the world or joined on the click meant to start typing (or on each keystroke). A field now acts on Enter only.
- **Added:** `uiplug.GameUI.Inject` (edit each frame's UI input from frame code: scripted menu tests) and `gogame.TakeJoinError` (why the menu's last join failed).
- **Added:** connected textures (`blocktex/connected.go`, `mesh.ConnectedProvider`, `BlockTextures.ConnectedLayers`): a project that gives the variants `X_ctm_0..15` of a block texture X gets, on each face of the block, the variant of the mask of its neighbours of the same block in the face's plane as seen on the texture (1 left, 2 right, 4 top, 8 bottom): a window of glass blocks has one frame around it instead of a grid. Test `TestConnectedTextureVariants`.
- **Fixed:** screen-space reflections of the water were almost never seen: the hit faded with the march step (to zero for far objects) and with rays along the view (0.25 for water seen at a low angle, the usual case). Now only the screen edge, rays coming back toward the camera and the last 30 % of the march fade it; the reflection ray uses half of the wave normal (the banks no longer break up into scattered texels); 6 refinement halvings (was 4). Banks and trees are mirrored in a river.
- **Changed:** a lighter view bob, like Minecraft's: one dip every 1.6 blocks walked (`bobStride`, was 0.95: the head nodded almost twice as often), no stronger when running (gain capped at the walk), gaze dip 0.4° and sway 0.2° (were 0.55° and 0.3°). Test `TestViewBobIsLightLikeMinecraft`.
- **Fixed:** walking judder: the controller advances the physics by fixed 1/120 s steps and the camera took the position of the last step, so at a frame rate that does not divide 120 (45 fps: 2 or 3 steps per frame) the eye moved 50 % more on one frame than on the next. The drawn eye (`frame`) and the view bob now follow the feet interpolated between the last two steps (`drawnFeet`, `ipFrom`/`ipTo`), at most one step (8 ms) behind; a position set outside the steps (teleport, `SetPos`, prediction) draws as it is. Test `TestEyeMovesEvenlyBetweenPhysicsSteps`.
- **Added:** `RenderSettings.WeatherFog` (`Renderer.SetWeatherFog`): multiplier of the fog the weather brings (fog episodes, the grey of rain and snow) and of how much land it may hide (0 = 1, < 0 = none); a fog episode at 1 cut the view to ~80 blocks. Test `TestWeatherFogSetting`.
- **Fixed:** texture blend between two blend classes (sand and gravel) frayed both ways: each side showed a strip of the other's texture on either side of a straight seam. A class block now receives only from a class listed before its own in `blend.json` (`blendMask`, `mesh/mesh.go`). Test `TestBlendBetweenTwoClassesGoesOneWay`.

- **Fixed:** hardening of the hardware ray tracing path and of the haze, after reports of a darker cone on Windows (not reproduced): the ray query loop of `rtTrace` (`shaders/rt.glsl`) is bounded to 384 candidate bricks per ray (the hardware has no step cap: a grazing ray across many chunks could run long enough for the driver's watchdog; a cut ray reports `rtStop` 1, "no information", like the software walk), the TLAS instances are written in slot order instead of map order (`render/vulkan/rtrq.go`: random chunks would have been dropped past `rqInstances`, and two builds differed), and `hazeHeight` (`atmo.glsl`, `rt_composite.comp`) never falls below 0.4, so the ground under a summit or a flier is not much clearer, hence darker, than the rest. Every shader recompiled (`make shaders`).
- **Fixed:** colours over-saturated since the radiance cache (ray traced GI, ultra level): under the sky the cached light is warmer than the hemispheric ambient it replaces (it carries the colour of the surfaces it bounced on, and the lit surface multiplies it by its own colour again), and the blue fill that kept warm materials from going orange was lost (grey stone turned brown). `ambientOf` (`shaders/voxel_body.glsl`) now keeps the cache's brightness but takes its colour from the hemispheric ambient, keeping `S.giHdr2.w` of its own (`BURROW_RT_GI_SAT`, default 0.15, `giSat` in `render/vulkan/rtgi.go`; 1 = the raw cache); out of the sky's reach (`skyOcc` 0: caves, rooms) it keeps all its colour, so magma and crystal still bleed. Measured on the demo platform (mean HSV saturation of the ground): 0.31 without ray tracing, 0.37 with it before, 0.35 after at 0.15. Shaders `voxel*`/`glass*` recompiled.

- **Fixed:** fine water stuttered and lagged on a dedicated server. A chunk's fine water changes every tick while it flows, and a client got a brick delta only when it held the version just before the current one; one frame without room for the chunk (or a slow link) and it fell two versions behind, so the server sent the whole chunk (up to thousands of bricks), which used more of the budget and made it fall further behind. Each chunk now keeps its last 64 deltas (`fineHistory`, `fineChunk.hist`) and `deltaFrom` merges the missed ones into a single delta (bricks that changed, cells that lost theirs), falling back to the whole chunk only past that history or when the merge is over the wire limit. Same wire format. Test `TestFineDeltaChainMergesMissedVersions`. 
- **Added:** falling streams of fine water are replicated (protocol version 4: `wire.RepFrame.StreamsSet`/`Streams`, `FineStreamEntry`, `MaxFineStreams`): a client used to see a fall only once its water landed (the curtain, the lip and the foot were missing). The server sends the list of streams whose lip is in the client's range when it changed (quantised like `syncFine`'s re-mesh digest, `streamKey`), and the client's `fineReplica` exports them with its bricks, so the voxel streamer meshes the cascade as on the server. Tests `TestFineWaterFallingStreamsReplicated`, wire round trip and limits (`wire_test.go`), golden Hello bytes (version 4).
- **Added:** swimming where you look. `walker.Input.SwimLook` (look pitch in degrees, up positive; 0 = off): with Forward held and the eyes under a liquid, the vertical swim speed follows `sin(pitch)` up to `SwimSpeed` (looking down dives, looking up climbs), unless Up or Dive is held. The local controller (`app/controller.go`) passes its pitch; the server and the predicting client (`net/netsim/move.go`) pass the input's pitch and now set `Forward` from `MoveY > 0`, like the controller. Test `TestPlayerSwimsWhereItLooks`.

- **Added:** `gogame.Game.ConfirmClose` (and `game.Window.ConfirmClose`), passed to `engine.WindowPlugin.ConfirmClose` for the title run and the network client: asked when the user closes the window (red button, Cmd+Q, Alt+F4), false keeps the window and the game running so that the game saves its world and then quits by itself (`Frame.Quit`). Burrow uses it to save the single-player world before the window closes (`kit/worlds/leave.go`).
- **Added:** grid gestures in `gameui` (`gameui/ui.go`, test `gameui/bag_gestures_test.go`): Shift+click on a filled cell emits `quick` without picking the item up; a right click picks half of a stack (`select`, `Value` "half"; the next placement's `move` has `Value` "half"), puts one item of the carried stack on a cell (`move`, `Value` "one"; it stays carried while some remain) or puts the carried item back; the carried item released after a drag, or clicked out, over the backdrop of the input screens (inside the window, outside every widget but layout stacks) emits `drop` (`Value` "one" for a right click). A carried stack emptied by the game stops being carried. `Input.Shift`/`Input.Ctrl` (set by `uiplug`), and `Input.Down/Up` now carry the right button. **Changed:** a drag released over the backdrop used to be cancelled silently; it now emits `drop` (ignored by grids that do not handle it).
- **Added:** `"repeat": true` on a button: held, it clicks after 0.4 s, then every 0.16 s down to 0.05 s; its release adds no click.

- **Changed:** movement authority, as in Minecraft. A predicting client now sends with every input where its own walk put the player (`netsim.Input` `px/py/pz/pvy/hp/tp`, `netsim.WithClaim`) and the server takes that position when it is plausible (`net/netsim/authority.go`, `claimOK`): a horizontal distance budget refilled every tick at the fastest allowed speed (×1.4, one second of burst), the climb allowed off the ground, a liquid or a ladder (`Rise`: 1.25 jump heights plus a step), the vertical speed, and the body box swept from the node to the claim (vertical then horizontal, or the reverse) must reach it. Before, the server walked every input itself and the client was corrected (rolled back and replayed) as soon as the two disagreed. Now the server answers with a teleport (`netsim.Player.TP`, replicated in the public registry) only when it moved the node itself (a game rule: knockback, teleport, mount, respawn: the node is not where the last input left it, `Player.Last`) or refused a claim (it then walks that input itself); the inputs computed before the client saw the teleport are walked by the server, and the client (`internal/netplay/predict.go`) snaps and replays only on a new teleport number. Inputs without a claim (other clients, lockstep, tests) are walked as before. The registry encoding gains flags 8 (TP, Rise, Budget, BudgetTick) and 16 (Last), absent while zero: older states decode and hash unchanged. Tests `TestHonestClaimsAreNeverCorrected`, `TestCheatedClaimsAreRefused` (speed, wall, flight), `TestServerMoveIsATeleport`, `TestAuthorityStateRoundTrips`, `TestPredictionMatchesTheServerExactly` (claims).
- **Fixed:** a replicated client animated everything by the integer tick of the last server frame (`FrameState.Tick`, set by `ReplicaSetTick` when a frame arrives): rain and snow streaks, water waves and swell, swaying leaves, clouds and animated textures stood still on most frames and jumped when frames came, unevenly (measured on a client at ~107 frames per second: 81 % of frames without motion, 19 ticks/s ± 40). The renderer now draws with a smooth animation clock (`render/vulkan/animclock.go`, as a Minecraft client ticks its own time between the server's updates): it advances with the wall clock between ticks, follows the tick without going back, freezes at most 2 ticks past the last one, stays exactly on a fixed tick (tests, frozen screenshots) and snaps on a jump; same measure after: 0 % of frames still, 20.0 ticks/s ± 0.4. Test `TestAnimClockIsSmoothBetweenBurstyTicks`. Branch `gogame-smooth-anim-time`.
- **Fixed:** the weather of a replicated client (sent every 20 ticks) drew its day clock as received: the rain cells, which drift with the clock, and the sky moved 20 ticks at a time. `weather.Plugin` advances the drawn clock with the ticks between two states, only for a clock seen running at one per tick and at most 40 ticks past the last state (`clientClock`, `weather/plugin.go`). - **Added:** predicted blocks on a replicated client. `replica.Client.PredictBlocks` (`net/replica/predict_blocks.go`) writes a guess into the replicated world at the next `Poll` and remembers the server's block under it; before every server frame the guessed cells go back to that truth (the frame applies to the server's state exactly), after it the truth is read again and the guess written back until the server acknowledged a later input (plus 4 frames) or 1.5 s passed: the cell then keeps what the server says (the block if a rule wrote it, the old one if it refused). `gogame.Frame.PredictVoxels` (no-op alone), and the window twins of the rules' helpers on the replicated copy: `Frame.RaycastShaped`, `Frame.PlaceStates`, `Frame.ToggleStates` (`gogame/framepredict.go`); `gogame.Client.PredictVoxels` for windowless clients (tests). Only `At` reads it: state, hash and snapshots are unchanged. Test `TestClimateRainCells`.
- **Added:** `gogame.Ctx.Weather(x, y, z)` (the `weather.Local` of a block, for the rules), `Ctx.WeatherFront()` and `Ctx.SetWeather(weather.Set)` (a `weather_set` from the rules: a game that freezes the automatic fronts and starts its own).
- **Changed (performance):** the HDR main pass no longer draws all terrain with one discarding pipeline. The solid range of the chunks that are not cross-fading is drawn first with `voxel_hdr_solid.frag` (`NO_DISCARD`: a shader that may discard turns off the early depth test and the hidden surface removal of tile-based GPUs for everything it draws); the cut-out range (leaves, grass, flowers, custom planes) then gets a depth prepass (`voxel_hdr_pre.frag`, `DEPTH_PREPASS`: the alpha test alone, no colour written: `pipeDesc.noColor`) and is shaded at depth EQUAL without discard (`pipeDesc.depthEqual`), so each visible foliage pixel is shaded once; cross-fading chunks and the slice view keep the discarding pipeline. `BURROW_LEAF_PREPASS=0` turns the prepass off. Measured in a forest overview (M2 Max, 1280x720, ultra): 22-24 ms GPU -> 14.3 ms (solid split alone: -1.2 ms), images identical; the low/medium non-HDR levels are unchanged. Tried and dropped (no measurable gain): back-face culling in the shadow pass, skipping the sun shadow taps for empty cut-out texels.
- **Added:** custom block planes attached to a face (`plane_cull` in `blocks/custom_blocks.json`, `shape.CustomSpec.PlaneCull`): such a plane is hidden when a solid neighbour covers that face and lit as that face; a plane lying flat on the whole face is drawn single-sided, facing out, and stays drawn next to another such block (Minecraft's fancy leaves: through the holes the deeper leaves show); a tilted plane attached to a face (`Quad.Tuft`) is also hidden when the neighbour has planes attached to its facing side (`Model.Shell`), so tufts show only where the face is in the open. Such planes cover nothing (a trunk behind holey leaves keeps its faces). `quadHidden` takes the footprint of a plane that leaves the cell within the face. Test `TestPlanesAttachedToAFaceHideBetweenNeighbours`.
- **Added:** connected textures per face (`mesh.ConnectedFaceProvider`, `BlockTextures.ConnectedFaceLayers`): a block without whole-block variants whose face texture X has `X_ctm_0..15` (a grass block's top, its dirt bottom) takes them on that face only, faces with a tinted overlay excepted; the face keeps its tint (biome), where whole-block variants are untinted. The variants of one texture are shared by every block.
- **Added:** `round` (custom blocks, `shape.CustomSpec.Round`, `DeriveRound`): a cube whose open edges are chamfered by that many sixteenths, 64 variants keyed by which faces are closed (a solid face, or another block with attached planes): an open face is inset along each edge it shares with another open face, a bevel covers that edge, a corner triangle closes three open faces; a face closed by such a neighbour stays whole (seen through the holes of a cut-out texture), so two blocks side by side show no groove. Every quad is attached to its face (lit as it, AO); the block has Shell on all faces. Test `TestRoundBlocksChamferOnlyOpenEdges`. The chamfers carry the normal of one of their faces (six normals only): a foliage fragment offsets its shadow lookup toward the sun instead of along its face (`voxel_body.glsl`), or the chamfers shadowed themselves (streaks along the edges and corners of round leaves). A bevel maps the texture at its own scale (a window as wide as the bevel; the whole texture squeezed into a strip drew stretched streaks along every edge). The cut-out mip bias (`CutoutMipBias`) is not applied to a project's foliage (`vFoliage`), whose leaf faces are nearly full: the earlier mips smeared them into streaks at grazing angles. Only the horizontal edges (with the top or the bottom) are chamfered (`roundVertical` off: the narrow bevels of the vertical edges, seen slantwise and moved by the wind, flickered without a temporal AA, ~300 flickering pixels a frame against ~80 with sharp leaves; now ~78). Where the neighbour across the end of a chamfered edge is not chamfered along it (a block over one of the two faces), the bevel stops short and the block keeps a square corner flush with it (`Model.RoundQuads`, square bits from `Mesher.roundSquare`, geometry cached per key).
- **Added:** `plane_cover` (custom blocks, `shape.CustomSpec.PlaneCover`): opaque planes lying flat on the faces (`plane_cull`) cover those faces, so nothing is drawn between two such blocks and a neighbour's face against them neither (a dense leaf cube draws its skin only). Test `TestPlaneCoverHidesFacesBetweenNeighbours`.
- **Fixed:** the soft sun shadow of the shader levels rotated its taps by a per-pixel noise that only a temporal anti-aliasing averages; without one (SMAA, FXAA, off) every penumbra showed a fine checker that crawled with the camera (plant and leaf shadows were all checker). A first try lighting foliage regardless of its facing (as the Minecraft shader packs do) was dropped: crowns came out flat.
- **Added:** `worldgen.CurrentSource` (`CurrentAt(seed, x, y, z) (fx, fz, ok)`): a generator says which way its still water runs. - **Fixed:** walking judder: the controller advances the physics by fixed 1/120 s steps and the camera took the position of the last step, so at a frame rate that does not divide 120 (45 fps: 2 or 3 steps per frame) the eye moved 50 % more on one frame than on the next. The drawn eye (`frame`) and the view bob now follow the feet interpolated between the last two steps (`drawnFeet`, `ipFrom`/`ipTo`), at most one step (8 ms) behind; a position set outside the steps (teleport, `SetPos`, prediction) draws as it is. - **Fixed:** colours over-saturated since the radiance cache (ray traced GI, ultra level): under the sky the cached light is warmer than the hemispheric ambient it replaces (it carries the colour of the surfaces it bounced on, and the lit surface multiplies it by its own colour again), and the blue fill that kept warm materials from going orange was lost (grey stone turned brown). `ambientOf` (`shaders/voxel_body.glsl`) now keeps the cache's brightness but takes its colour from the hemispheric ambient, keeping `S.giHdr2.w` of its own (`BURROW_RT_GI_SAT`, default 0.15, `giSat` in `render/vulkan/rtgi.go`; 1 = the raw cache); out of the sky's reach (`skyOcc` 0: caves, rooms) it keeps all its colour, so magma and crystal still bleed. - **Fixed:** fine water stuttered and lagged on a dedicated server. A chunk's fine water changes every tick while it flows, and a client got a brick delta only when it held the version just before the current one; one frame without room for the chunk (or a slow link) and it fell two versions behind, so the server sent the whole chunk (up to thousands of bricks), which used more of the budget and made it fall further behind. Each chunk now keeps its last 64 deltas (`fineHistory`, `fineChunk.hist`) and `deltaFrom` merges the missed ones into a single delta (bricks that changed, cells that lost theirs), falling back to the whole chunk only past that history or when the merge is over the wire limit. Same wire format. Test `TestFineDeltaChainMergesMissedVersions`. 
- **Added:** falling streams of fine water are replicated (protocol version 4: `wire.RepFrame.StreamsSet`/`Streams`, `FineStreamEntry`, `MaxFineStreams`): a client used to see a fall only once its water landed (the curtain, the lip and the foot were missing). The server sends the list of streams whose lip is in the client's range when it changed (quantised like `syncFine`'s re-mesh digest, `streamKey`), and the client's `fineReplica` exports them with its bricks, so the voxel streamer meshes the cascade as on the server. Tests `TestFineWaterFallingStreamsReplicated`, wire round trip and limits (`wire_test.go`), golden Hello bytes (version 4).

The local controller (`app/controller.go`) passes its pitch; the server and the predicting client (`net/netsim/move.go`) pass the input's pitch and now set `Forward` from `MoveY > 0`, like the controller. Test `TestPlayerSwimsWhereItLooks`.

A carried stack emptied by the game stops being carried. `Input.Shift`/`Input.Ctrl` (set by `uiplug`), and `Input.Down/Up` now carry the right button. **Changed:** a drag released over the backdrop used to be cancelled silently; it now emits `drop` (ignored by grids that do not handle it).

- **Added:** radiance cache, the ray traced GI of the HDR levels (`render/vulkan/rtgi.go`, `shaders/gi.glsl`, `rt_gi.comp`; docs/ray-tracing.md "Radiance cache"): a toroidal grid of 128 x 64 x 128 one-block cells around the camera keeps, per air cell and axis direction, the radiance arriving on the voxel face behind it (52 MiB). Every frame `rt_gi.comp` refreshes half the grid (`BURROW_RT_GI_STRIDE`, default 2) with 2 rays per visible face (`BURROW_RT_GI_RAYS`); a hit is lit by the sun (shadow ray), the particle lights, its emission and the cache in front of it, so light bounces once more each frame (multi-bounce by feedback). the lit voxel shaders read it per fragment (bilinear over the valid cells of the layer in front of the face, faded out at the grid's edge, times `BURROW_RT_GI_GAIN`, default 0.75) and take it as their ambient in place of the hemispheric sky light attenuated by the propagated skylight: caves are lit by what really reaches them (magma, crystal, the opening), with colour bleeding. Faces of shaped solid blocks count (`render.RTSurface`: a material byte without occupancy, so the stairs, walls and models of a dungeon are lit and rays pass through them), and the emitters rays cannot hit (torches, lanterns, glowing plants: `RTBlocks.Light`, `RTChunk.Lights`) are sampled as point lights with a shadow ray at each hit (set 1 binding 7), following the propagated block light's falloff so a torch's bounce matches its raster light. Set 0 gains binding 2 (storage buffer, vertex + fragment + compute; a 64 byte placeholder while the cache is off) and the scene UBO `giHdr`/`giHdr2` (floats 680..687). With the cache on, the per-pixel GI ray and the composite's GI ratio are off (`BURROW_RT_GI=screen` restores them). `BURROW_RT_DEBUG=7` shows the cached irradiance (magenta = no data).
- **Added:** hardware ray tracing (`render/vulkan/rtrq.go`, `third_party_vulkan/rt_khr.go` + `rt_khr_decl.h`; docs/ray-tracing.md "Hardware path"): on a device with `VK_KHR_acceleration_structure`, `VK_KHR_ray_query`, `VK_KHR_deferred_host_operations` and the acceleration structure, ray query and buffer device address features (NVIDIA RTX, AMD RX 6000+, Intel Arc), the device is created with them (`ctx.rtHW`; `BURROW_RT_HW=0` keeps the software tracer) and the tracer adds a BLAS per chunk slot (64 AABBs, one per 8^3 brick, inactive where the brick has no occluder) and a TLAS of the occupied slots, rebuilt in the frame of any change. `rt_trace_rq.comp` and `rt_gi_rq.comp` (SPIR-V 1.4, `SHADERS_RQ` in the Makefile) let the hardware find the bricks and walk the voxels inside (`rt.glsl` `RT_RAYQUERY`). Any failure at setup or pipeline creation falls back to the software tracer. **Not run yet on hardware** (MoltenVK has no such extension): unit tests check the AABB and instance layouts and the SPIR-V capabilities.

- **Fixed:** the ground seen from high above came out white (HDR levels, with or without ray tracing): the distance fog that hides the edge of the streamed world used the 3D distance, so from a summit or from the sky the ground below was beyond the fog's end; it now follows the horizontal distance (`edgeFog`: the world streams whole columns). The aerial perspective took the same density all along the ray; its optical depth now falls off with the height above the ray's lowest point (`hazeHeight`, scale height 48 blocks): unchanged for a level ray, much clearer looking down from high. `atmo.glsl` `hdrFinish` (terrain, water, meshes, particles) and the ray tracing composite's fade.
- **Fixed:** the ray tracing preset of the shader level was frozen at start: `RenderSettings.RT` stored the resolved preset ("off" for a medium start), which then counted as an explicit choice, so a game that switched to ultra in its options never turned ray tracing on. Nobody chose (no flag, no `BURROW_RT`): `RT` stays "" and follows the level.

- **Fixed:** the traced sun shadow blackened caves (`shadows` and `full`): the composite estimated the sun's share of a pixel as if it saw the hemispheric ambient and the full sun, so in a cave whose sun the skylight gate had already removed it darkened every sunward face to black. The lit voxel shaders now write 1 - the exact share of the direct sun (diffuse, specular, leaf glow, after the shadow map and the skylight gate) into the alpha of the HDR target (`gSun`, `finishColor` in `voxel_body.glsl`) and the composite scales that share (`rt_composite.comp`). A blended pass drawn later can only raise the alpha (less traced shadow, never black); meshes write 1 (they keep the shadow map of hybrid frames).
- **Fixed:** Vulkan validation error `VUID-vkCmdBeginRendering-pRenderingInfo-09592` every frame with ray tracing on: the composite set `rgRes.storage` on the HDR target for good, so any later graph pass that rendered into it got a barrier to GENERAL and began rendering in the wrong layout. Storage writes are now per pass (`renderGraph.addStorage`).

- **Fixed:** a chunk meshed from the provisional light estimate (the light field was busy somewhere, streaming suffices) kept that estimate for good when the light around it had already settled: re-meshes after a relight are decided only for chunks next to a cell whose light changed, and nothing changed any more. The estimate reads the padded chunk only, so a floor on the top layer of a chunk (y = 31 mod 32), lit by a torch two blocks up in the chunk above, stayed black under a lit room. Every mesh now records `mesh.Result.LightSum` (block channels and skylight added up, `mesh.LightSums`); a mesh built from the estimate is judged against the field once it is idle and re-meshed only when the difference is clear (`mesh.LightFar`: more than a twentieth and more than a few cells' worth), so open ground meshed early costs ~10 % more uploads (`TestLightStreamingUploadsStayLow`: 1.10x) instead of re-meshing everything. `lightRunner.record` takes the estimated flag and the sums (`engine/lightrun.go`, `engine/voxelstream.go`). Test `TestEstimatedMeshIsCheckedWhenIdle`.

- **Fixed:** fine water under a body of water was treated like water at the surface. A cell dug under the sea floor kept 6.5/8 of water forever (the source above topped it to `FineSourceLevel`, 2/8 per sub-cell, never more), with a visible surface and an air gap inside the sea; a block broken inside the sea never rested (the source above poured, the body sources beside absorbed down to `FineBodyLevel`: 1.5 million units created and drained in 4000 ticks) and, once fixed, stayed three bricks for ever; a tunnel dug sideways from the sea stopped at the body level (6/8) and then at 92 % under its rock ceiling; a closed cave opened under the sea folded a level short of its ceiling. Rules (fine_step.go): a body source with a source above it feeds at a full block (`sourceHead`); a body source tops the brick under it up to full once the water below can fall no further; a body source beside a submerged brick (`submergedAt`: bricks and full cells up to a source) feeds the whole layer; a brick under a ceiling joined through water to a submerged source is topped up to its ceiling (`confinedUnder`); the pressure pass takes a body source on top of (or a submerged source beside) a body of full cells as an inexhaustible front that gives the whole difference; a full coarse cell beside a body source is at rest when submerged (`calmBeside`, coarse predicate and fold). Floating springs keep their behaviour. A breach low in a bank onto open ground now floods a larger sheet (`TestFineSourceAndSeaLedger`: limit 80000 ticks, rest at ~63000). `FineRules` = 5 (older snapshots restore and continue; a journal recorded under version 4 fails its first hash check). Tests `fluid/fine_submerged_test.go`; `docs/water-fine.md` § "Water under a body of water".

- **Added:** sealed games. `pak.Seal` / `pak.Unseal` encrypt a whole `.voxpak` with AES-256-GCM (`"BRWSEAL1" nonce ciphertext`, the header is the associated data: a changed or wrong-key file is refused with `pak.ErrSealed`). `gogame.Game.SealedPack` (file next to the executable) + `SealKey` make `Main` read every project file from that archive when it exists (`game.UseSealed`, `game.OpenSealed`, `Source.Sealed`): it is decrypted once, verified, and mounted in memory; nothing is extracted to disk, so the distributed folder holds no readable model, texture or sound. Absent file = the project directory as before. The project hash (multiplayer pins) is computed over the same plaintext files, so a sealed server and a sealed client agree. Hot reload is off for a sealed game. The key lives in the executable: this stops casual reading and standard tools, not someone who runs the game and dumps its memory.
- **Added:** package `vfs`: `Mount` serves a `Source` (a `pak.Reader` through `NewPakSource`) under a virtual absolute directory that does not exist on disk; `ReadFile`, `Open`, `Stat`, `Lstat`, `ReadDir`, `WalkDir`, `EvalSymlinks`, `DirFS`, `SameFile`, `OpenUnder` answer from memory for a path under the mount (or a relative path that names a mounted file) and call the `os` function otherwise, so saves and settings still go to the disk. Without a mount every function is the plain `os` call. The engine's project file reads use it: `assets` (`safepath`, `db`, `project`, `blocktex/overrides`), `audio/soundpack` (`OpenFile` on both platforms, guard, scan, config), `level/library`, `script/datastore`, `internal/game` (`Source.Path/Read`, scene and audio scans, net pins, UI discovery). Tests: `vfs/vfs_test.go`.

- Ragged texture blend between neighbouring blocks: `<project>/textures/blend.json` (`classes`: up to 7 untinted block texture
  names, `over`: other receivers). The top face of a receiver next to a class block of another texture carries `mesh.Vertex.Blend`

  the spare bits of z (10-13) and w (13-15) of the chunk vertex, and `voxel_body.glsl` draws the class texture along those edges
  with a three-octave noise limit. The class layers ride in the animation table (x = -1000 - class). Test `TestBlendEdgesOnTopFaces`. `blocktex.SetBlendEnabled(bool)` (graphics option): a change bumps `OverrideGeneration`, so the table is rebuilt and the world re-meshed.
- Anti-tiling: `blend.json` `scatter` lists blocks whose top and bottom textures are mirrored in u and/or v and transposed (8 variants, normals follow) per world cell, with a slow brightness drift, and a seam mix: within 0.16 block of a cell edge the texture of the cell across it is blended in (up to half at the edge) (`mesh.ScatterProvider`, `Vertex.Scatter`, z bit 14, `voxel_body.glsl`: view, light and normal follow the mirror). Same on/off switch as the blend.
- `voxel_body.glsl`: no parallax march on any cut-out texture (top mip not opaque), tinted or not, and the alpha-coverage compensation of distant mips applies to them too: a project's foliage with its colour baked in (custom 3D leaves, grass blades) shimmered.

# Changelog

Detailed history before 0.1.0: [docs/changelog-history.md](docs/changelog-history.md).
- **Added:** `engine.FrameFX`, a frame-domain resource through which a game drives each frame (host code: `engine.TryRes[*engine.FrameFX]`) a colour grade and local mist volumes; the Vulkan render plugin inserts it and pushes it to the renderer every frame (`Renderer.SetFrameFX`). `render.Grade` is a lift / gamma / gain applied after tone mapping in `post_final.frag` (zero = neutral, clamped). `render.Mist` is an ellipsoid of fog (centre, radius, squash, colour, density, glow) whose density falls from the centre to the edge; its optical depth is integrated analytically along each view ray (`mistApply` in `atmo.glsl`, called by `hdrFinish` and the HDR sky): it absorbs what lies behind and glows with its colour, additive particles only lose light. At most `render.MaxMist` (4) volumes, the nearest to the camera. Scene UBO grows to 2816 bytes (floats 620..679, declared in `common.glsl` and `scene3d.glsl`); no scene component, so registry and state hashes are unchanged. The soft renderer ignores both. Test `TestFrameFXUniforms`.
- **Added:** HDR sprite tints (Vulkan): a `render.sprite` colour component above 1 is a brightness boost. The texture is tinted by `color / boost` and clamped as before, then multiplied by the boost after the conversion to linear, so on an HDR target the sprite exceeds 1 and feeds the bloom (glowing decals, shock rings, light pools). Tints at or below 1 render exactly as before (`shaders/sprite.frag`). The soft renderer still clamps.
- **Added:** `gogame.Frame.PlaySound(emitter, sound, SoundOpts)`, the Frame twin of `Ctx.PlaySound`: a network client plays a sound the server asked for (a dedicated server runs no audio device, and `OnTick` only runs there). It builds the same `audio.SoundEvent` (same checks, mode, bus, priority; handle derived from emitter, tick and order) and queues it for the next frame with `engine.Send`, never journaled, silent without the audio plugin. A game carries the request in the player's data like the other client effects. Test `TestFramePlaySound`.
- **Added:** `gogame.Frame.SetMusicContext(ctx)` and `audioplug.Audio.MusicContext`: a network client takes the music context its server decides (`"boss"`, `"dungeon_crypt"`, any `music.<name>` of the sound pack, `""` for the automatic day / night / cave). The `audio.music` component is scene data that is not replicated (only the components in the state hash are), so the server could not patch it for a window; the override replaces the context of the `audio.music` entity in effect for this client (a copy: the component is untouched), until the next call. Names are limited to `a-z A-Z 0-9 _ . -`, 64 bytes. Tests `TestFrameSetMusicContext`, `TestWithMusicContext`.

- **Added:** `engine.RenderSettings.Parallax` (depth in blocks of the normal-map height channel on near faces, 0 = default, < 0 = off) and live application of `NormalStrength`, `SpecBoost` and `Parallax` by the Vulkan `RenderPlugin`: until now `RenderSettings.NormalStrength/SpecBoost` were read only at start and by the soft renderer, so a game that set them at run time changed nothing on screen. A change is applied once at the next frame (`Renderer.SetPBRStrength` / `SetParallax`, through `RenderSettings.pbrChanged`); the F6 preset now goes through the same path (it sets the three fields instead of calling the renderer). Test `TestRenderSettingsPBRChangedReportsOncePerChange`.
- **Added:** project blocks (`runtime.custom_blocks`) accept `"planes"`: textured quads `[x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, x2,y2,z2, x3,y3,z3]` (four corners in sixteenths of a block, bottom corners first, coordinates -16..32, at most 64) drawn instead of the model boxes, double-sided with the whole texture. A plane may leave the cell and be tilted, so a block of foliage can be a cluster of leaf planes that hides the cubic grid; the boxes remain the collision and the selection (planes need a model), a plane model hides no neighbour face, and with `facing` the planes turn with the boxes. `shape.CustomSpec.Planes`, `shape.ValidatePlanes`, `shape.MaxCustomPlanes`. The mesher holds a shape quad vertex at the chunk's edge instead of letting it go negative (the GPU keeps a position in 10 bits: a negative one wrapped to the far side of the chunk and drew a streak across the view; only a plane poking out of a block on the chunk edge is flattened). Tests `TestPlaneOvershootNeverGoesNegativeAtTheChunkEdge`, `TestCustomPlanesAreTheLookAndTheBoxesTheCollision`, `TestCustomPlanesTurnWithFacing`, `TestCustomPlanesValidation`.
- **Fixed:** on a network client (predicted controller) the sprint field of view widening stuck on after a double-tap forward and never came with the sprint key: the sprint state is kept by the physics step, which a predicted controller does not run, so nothing ever cleared it (the camera stayed pulled back after running). `Update` now keeps the state for a predicted controller with the same rules (sprint while forward is held and the sprint key is down, ends on release or on sneaking). Test `TestSprintFOVOnAPredictedController`.
